newsitem.title: USA: IBM, oil earnings to dominate stock market.
newsitem.headline: IBM, oil earnings to dominate stock market.

text.p: After a week that saw stocks bounce back after steep losses, corporate earnings will again dominate Wall Street this week, with the spotlight on heavyweight International Business Machines Corp.
Investors will focus on earnings, particularily in the absence of any important economic data aside from March exisiting home sales, which are due out on Friday.
Along with IBM, which is expected to report after the close of trading Wednesday, major U.S. oil companies will also be posting their first quarter results.

"People are attuned to an earnings disappointment in IBM," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "If it comes in flat or slightly lower than forecast, it's no big deal. But the stock could move on a surprsingly good quarter.
"Then again, if it's terrible, that's something we are not ready for," he said.
One the 30 components of the Dow Jones industrial average, news from the computer giant can often inspire or depress the broader market.
The Dow ended Friday with a gain of 44.95 points at 6,703.55. It rose 311.86 points for the week, the biggest weekly gain in the index's history.
Before last week's rebound, the selloff in U.S. stocks had knocked nearly 700 points off the Dow from its March 11 high at 7,085.16.
According to First Call, IBM is expected to report first quarter earnings per share of $2.28 compared to $2.21 a year ago.

Some analysts have said that IBM could beat analysts' estimates. Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones said on April 11 that the company could come close to earnings of $2.35 per share, his estimate for the quarter.
Also reporting this week are oil companies, including Texaco Inc., Exxon Corp., Amoco Corp., Chevron Corp. and Mobil Corp.
"Most on the Street have the oils in their sights," Wachtel said. "With the techs it's hard to pin down the earnings. With oil stocks you can do it to the penny. They offer very few surprises."
Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said that we was looking for a pullback this week.
"We are due for some kind of pullback this week," Harrington said. "It would be very positive if volume could thin out during a pullback. It would indicate some drying up of selling pressure.
"If we see a selloff on heavy volume and secondary stocks join blue chips on the way down, it will not be a good sign for the market in the coming weeks."
